events.note: 9 September 1945: the US Army Military Government takes the south of Korea. USAMGIK page: it ruled 'the southern half of the Korean Peninsula' from 9 September 1945 to 15 August 1948. Japan's ledger/77 hands Korea south of the 38th parallel to the United States in 1945, so the US holds the land when the found event runs: the found event moved 1 cell and the US keyframe_1945 then released 517 cells to nobody, so South Korea was nobody's land from 1945 to 1948. This takes the land from the US holder.

events.note: 2 August 1940: the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic is established on the main part of the annexed Bessarabia. Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina page: 'on 2 August 1940, the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic was established on the main part of the annexed territory'. The Union took Bessarabia from Romania in June-July 1940 (union ledger/16), so the republic's own founding (ledger/0) found only the 18 cells of the Moldavian ASSR; this gain from the Union gives it the Bessarabian land it was founded on (112 cells), in the month the page gives. events.note: 2 August 1940: Northern Bukovina, Hertsa and the Budjak counties are allotted to the Ukrainian SSR. Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina page: the Soviet commission 'allotted Northern Bukovina, Hertsa region and larger parts of Hotin' and the Ismail and Cetatea Alba counties to the Ukrainian SSR, while 'smaller portions were given to the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic' from the annexed land. The Union took the land from Romania in June 1940 (union ledger/16) and held it direct, so the republic's own gain (ledger/36) found little; this gain from the Union hands over the rest (about 80 cells) in August. (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026.)

region.text: Ukraine within its 1954-1991 borders: the land the Union holds directly inside the Ukrainian SSR after the 1943 reconquest

events.note: 1944: the Ukrainian SSR holds the land the Red Army reclaimed in the Battle of the Dnieper (26 August to 23 December 1943). Battle of the Dnieper page: 'Soviets reclaim left-bank Ukraine, including the city of Kiev and Donets basin'. The Union's own gains of 1943 (union ledger/30 and /31, and the year-end snap of its 1943 shape, p1940-p1949 keyframe_overrides/0) took that land as Union-direct land, and the Ukrainian SSR's occupation_end events (ledger/42-45) found nothing to give back. Bridging: the snap lies at the end of 1943, so January 1944, the month after the battle ended, is the first month the compile can hand the land to the republic. Only Union-held cells move (about 1,000); that includes the core of the republic that the Union has held direct since its 1922 founding gain (union ledger/0, window p1920-p1929), which the republic has held again since this event. (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026.)

region.text: Belarus within the borders of 1939-1991: the land the Union holds directly after Bagration

events.note: August 1944: Operation Bagration ends and the whole Byelorussian SSR is again the republic's land. Operation Bagration page: 'a military campaign fought between 22 June and 19 August 1944 in Soviet Byelorussia'; infobox 'Red Army retakes all of Byelorussian SSR'; 'Minsk liberated on 4 July'. The Union's gain of July 1944 (union ledger/34) took the land from Germany and Ostland as Union-direct land (588 cells), and the Byelorussian SSR's own occupation_end (ledger/16) found nothing to give back for it. This gain from the Union hands the Union-held land of Belarus (753 cells with the core held since 1922) to the republic in August 1944, when the campaign ended. (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026.)

region.text: Moldova, the Moldavian SSR with Transnistria: the land the Union holds directly after the reoccupation of Bessarabia

events.note: September 1944: after the Second Jassy-Kishinev offensive (20 to 29 August) Soviet control over Bessarabia is re-established and the Moldavian SSR holds it again. Second Jassy-Kishinev offensive page: 'Soviet control over Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina, which had been occupied by the USSR in 1940, was re-established'. The Union's gain of August 1944 (union ledger/35) and the snap of its 1945 shape kept Moldova as Union-direct land (111 cells) and the republic's occupation_end (ledger/3) found only 1; this gain from the Union gives it back in September, the first month after the offensive ended. (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026.)

region.text: Lithuania within Natural Earth borders: the south and centre of Lithuania that Ostland's ledger never gives back

events.note: November 1944: the Baltic offensive (14 September to 24 November) ends with German forces expelled from Lithuania, and the last Lithuanian land under Ostland returns to the Lithuanian SSR. Baltic offensive page: 14 September to 24 November 1944; 'The Baltic offensive operation resulted in the expulsion of German forces from Estonia and Lithuania'. Ostland's ledger gives back Vilnius, Kaunas and Samogitia (ledger/5, /6, /9), but 115 cells of southern Lithuania stayed Ostland's after the republic's occupation_end (ledger/2, October 1944, which names Germany, not Ostland) and were drawn as the Reichskommissariat's land through 1945 until the year-end snap of the Union's 1945 shape took them as Union-direct land. Confidence 2: the page dates the offensive, not the clearing of southern Lithuania. (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026.)

region.text: Ukraine within its 1954-1991 borders: the Union-held cells of Northern Bukovina, Budjak and the Dniester border that the 1944 snap took

Second Jassy-Kishinev offensive page: 'Soviet control over Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina, which had been occupied by the USSR in 1940, was re-established' after the offensive of 20 to 29 August 1944. The year-end snap of the Union's 1944 shape took about 80 cells of Northern Bukovina, Budjak and the Dniester border as Union-direct land after the 1944-01 gain had run. Bridging: January 1945 is the first month the compile can follow a year-end snap. Confidence 2. (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026. Review sm-07: source set to the Jassy-Kishinev page, which holds the quoted sentence; the Bessarabia occupation page does not.)

region.text: Kazakhstan, the Kazakh SSR of 1936-1991: the Union-held cells inside it

events.note: 1945: the Kazakh SSR, a union republic since 5 December 1936, holds its whole land of 2,717,300 km2. keyframe_overrides.why: The 1943 shape is the front of early 1943; at its year-end snap the compile released 1,800 Soviet cells (Smolensk, Bryansk, Orel, Kursk, Kharkiv, Poltava, Kyiv ...) to nobody although the ledger and the pages have the Red Army holding them. Battle of the Dnieper page: the Soviets reclaimed 'left-bank Ukraine, including the city of Kiev and Donets basin' by 23 December 1943 while 'the west bank was still in German hands for the most part'; Eastern Front page: Orel 'retaken by the Red Army on 5 August 1943', Kharkov 'abandoned for the final time on 22 August'; Kursk page: 'Kursk was retaken by the Soviets on 8 February 1943'; Smolensk Operation page (7 August - 2 October 1943): Smolensk liberated 25 September, Soviet pincer around Bryansk 'forcing German forces to withdraw'. Kaluga, Tula, the west of Moscow Oblast and Lipetsk (204 cells nobody's at the snap) lie, by the cell centres of the gazetteer, north-east and east of Orel (retaken 5 August 1943) and east of Smolensk (liberated 25 September), behind the front of the whole second half of 1943; the dossier's own ledger/46 ends the German occupation of western and southern Russia in 1943 and the Smolensk and Orel pages put no German holding east of that line. Pskov, Novgorod, Leningrad Oblast, the west of Tver Oblast, Crimea, Krasnodar, right-bank Ukraine and Belarus stay outside (pages silent for the end of 1943). keyframe_overrides.why: The Cliopatria shape of 1949-1962 leaves 57 cells of Greece unowned (the south coast of Crete, the Peloponnese, Thrace, Central Greece, Attica and others), drawn as grey specks from 1949 to the start of the p1960 window, where p1960-p1969 events/2 and keyframe_overrides/0-1 take over; the correction keeps the shape's 10 cells outside the country polygon and adds the whole country. Greek junta page: 'On 21 April 1967, a group of colonels overthrew a caretaker government' and 'By the early morning hours, the whole of Greece was in the hands of the colonels', so until then the kingdom held the whole country; Dodecanese page: 'they were formally united with Greece by the 1947 Peace Treaty with Italy'; Greek Civil War page: the ceasefire of 16 October ended the war. Companion of p1960-p1969 keyframe_overrides/0 (the 1963 shape). (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026.)
